svg.title: Auction Format Yield Bands
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-07-auction-format-yield-bands; chapter number: 4; title: Auction Format Yield Bands; subtitle: The statutory rate is a ceiling; the format decides the real yield; chart type: stacked_comparison; total range: 0% to 18% depending on state and auction format; buckets: label: Florida Interest Bid-Down; low: 0.25; high: 18; notes: Quarter-point bids still collect the 5% penalty on fast redemption, but a quarter-point lien held two years yields only about 2.5% a year.; label: Arizona Proxy Bidding; low: 5; high: 16; notes: A lone 5% bid clears at the 16% maximum in proxy counties; in direct bid counties the same bid locks in 5%.; label: Colorado Premium Bidding; low: 13; high: 13; notes: About 13% in 2026, set at 9% over the federal discount rate, with a 3-year redemption period; confirm overbid treatment first.; label: New Jersey Bid-Down to Premium; low: 0; high: 18; notes: Bids run 18% to 0%, then flip into dollar premiums; large investors scoop up sales at 0%.; caption: Institutional money grinds popular counties toward zero, yet floors, proxy engines and fixed premium rates still leave pockets of real yield.; assumptions note: Yields assume redemption on the stated terms; operators split on whether quarter-point fast-five plays are smart bets or traps when liens sit unredeemed for years.; note: Sources: Tax Sale Resources (XbThUArmcIE @ 00:01:24, 00:02:11); Realauction (cleRXY7vybQ @ 00:02:20; hKsLdKqVOE0 @ 00:01:12); Tax Sale Secrets (stFlmSmpP3Q @ 00:01:09); Tax Lien School Highlights - Dustin Hahn (mHvzzGVcYdI @ 00:01:53); Tax Sale Academy (0I_mhnrF0So @ 00:02:42).
